questions.prompt: Reference feedforward is a second path from \(r\) into the command \(u\). It is used so that
questions.explanation: A prefilter or a feedforward path shapes how \(r\) enters, and it does not change the loop gain built from the feedback of \(y\). Redesigning \(L\) is what the feedback block does. Feedforward of \(r\) does not see sensor noise, and it does not move the closed-loop poles.

questions.prompt: A measured disturbance adds at the plant input. Its value is 1.6. The feedforward command that cancels it is
questions.explanation: The net input is \(u + d\). Cancellation needs \(u = -d = -1.6\). The choice \(+d\) pushes in the same direction as the disturbance. Dividing by the plant gain is the cancellation for a disturbance that adds at the output.

questions.prompt: A plant has DC gain 2.5. The static feedforward gain that inverts that plant at DC is
questions.explanation: Ideal static inversion uses \(F = 1/P = 1/2.5 = 0.4\). Using \(P\) itself, 2.5, amplifies the reference instead of inverting the plant. Using \(1 + P\) is the feedback sensitivity factor, not the inverse.

questions.prompt: A disturbance of size 2 adds at the plant output. The plant DC gain is 5. The input command that cancels that disturbance in steady state is
questions.explanation: An output disturbance \(d\) is cancelled by a plant input \(-d/P\). Here that is \(-2/5 = -0.4\). The command \(-d = -2\) would be right only if the disturbance added at the input. The command \(-P d = -10\) has the plant gain in the numerator.

questions.prompt: Adding a reference prefilter in front of an otherwise unchanged feedback loop
questions.explanation: The prefilter multiplies the reference and does not sit inside the loop, so \(L\) and the margins stay put. Poles of the loop are roots of \(1 + L = 0\) and do not move. A prefilter cannot create the infinite DC loop gain that an integrator provides, and \(S = 1/(1+L)\) is unchanged.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 354 120" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>reference feedforward</title><text x="24" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">in</text><line x1="42" y1="56" x2="78" y2="56"/><polygon points="78,56 71.6,58.7 71.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><rect x="78" y="34" width="84" height="44" rx="4" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.10"/><text x="120" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">F</text><line x1="162" y1="56" x2="198" y2="56"/><polygon points="198,56 191.6,58.7 191.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><rect x="198" y="34" width="84" height="44" rx="4" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.10"/><text x="240" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">P</text><line x1="282" y1="56" x2="318" y2="56"/><polygon points="318,56 311.6,58.7 311.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="322" y="60" text-anchor="start" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">out</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A block in front of a plant.
options: leaves the loop gain, and therefore the stability margins, unchanged
removes steady-state error even when the loop has no integrator
makes the sensitivity function identically zero

questions.prompt: The true plant DC gain is 10 and the model used for inversion has DC gain 8. With no feedback, the reference-to-output gain is
questions.explanation: Open-loop inversion sets \(F = 1/8\), so \(y/r = P F = 10/8 = 1.25\). Perfect inversion would give 1, which is what the model promised, not what the true plant does. The ratio \(8/10 = 0.8\) inverts the two gains.

questions.prompt: The same mismatched inverse is used, so a unit reference produces output 1.25 with no feedback. The steady error is 0.25 because
questions.explanation: \(P F = 1.25\), so the output sits 0.25 above a unit reference. That fraction is this particular mismatch, not a fixed property of feedforward. No feedback loop is present in this calculation, and sensor noise enters through \(S\), which was not in the path.
questions.figure_alt: A step that settles above the final command.
options: feedforward always leaves a 25 percent error
the true plant is larger than the model, so the output overshoots the reference

questions.prompt: A unity-feedback loop has complementary sensitivity \(T(0) = 0.75\). A reference prefilter \(F\) is placed in front of the loop. The DC value of \(F\) that makes the overall DC gain equal to 1 is
questions.explanation: The prefilter sees the closed-loop map, so the overall gain is \(F\, T(0)\). Setting that to 1 gives \(F = 1/0.75 = 1.33333\). Using \(T\) itself, 0.75, would make the overall gain \(0.5625\). Using \(1 - T = 0.25\) is the sensitivity, not the required prefilter.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 354 120" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>prefilter on a closed loop</title><text x="24" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">in</text><line x1="42" y1="56" x2="78" y2="56"/><polygon points="78,56 71.6,58.7 71.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><rect x="78" y="34" width="84" height="44" rx="4" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.10"/><text x="120" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">F</text><line x1="162" y1="56" x2="198" y2="56"/><polygon points="198,56 191.6,58.7 191.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><rect x="198" y="34" width="84" height="44" rx="4" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.10"/><text x="240" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">T</text><line x1="282" y1="56" x2="318" y2="56"/><polygon points="318,56 311.6,58.7 311.6,53.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="322" y="60" text-anchor="start" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">out</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A prefilter in series with a closed-loop block.

questions.prompt: A unity-feedback loop has DC loop gain \(L(0) = 6\), with \(L\) real and positive. The prefilter that restores overall DC gain 1, placed in front of this loop, has gain
questions.explanation: \(T(0) = L/(1+L) = 6/7\). The prefilter is \(1/T = 7/6 = 1.16667\). Using \(1 + L = 7\) ignores that most of the reference already gets through. Using \(L = 6\) is the loop gain, not the prefilter.

questions.prompt: A measured input disturbance is really 2, but the measurement used for cancellation reads 2.3. The feedforward command is \(-2.3\). The residual disturbance at the plant input is
questions.explanation: The plant input sees \(d + u = 2 - 2.3 = -0.3\). A perfect measurement would leave 0, which cannot be the graded value. The residual \(2.3 - 2 = +0.3\) has the sign of the measurement error rather than the sign of \(d + u\).

questions.prompt: A plant has a right-half-plane zero. A feedforward block that inverts the whole plant model
questions.explanation: Inverting a right-half-plane zero produces a right-half-plane pole, which is an unstable filter. Cancelling that zero with a stable pole is not inversion. Feedforward does not place the loop poles, and a full inverse of a non-minimum-phase plant is not a stable proper filter.

options: is always a stable, proper filter
can cancel that zero with a stable pole
moves the closed-loop poles into the left half-plane by itself
asks for an unstable or non-causal inverse, so only the stable part of the model is inverted

questions.prompt: Disturbance feedforward is perfect at DC and the feedback sensitivity at DC is \(S(0) = 0.12\). A unit output disturbance that is not measured still appears at the output with size
questions.explanation: Feedforward never sees an unmeasured disturbance, so the feedback path still passes it through \(S\). The output piece is \(0.12\). The complementary value \(1 - 0.12 = 0.88\) is \(T\), the reference map, not the disturbance map. Zero would require the disturbance to be measured and cancelled.
